title: Gear cadence and gold bars paint unreached levels as measured zeros
body:
## Summary
PowerTab's Gear Replacement Cadence and Average Gold bars draw every bracket, so a level no agent reached renders as a 2%-high '0 upgrades' / '0g' bar.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/economy-simulator/PowerRarityTabs.tsx:73 colours a zero-replacement bracket the same whether it was sampled or unreached (the engine writes gearReplacementCount 0 and avgGold 0 for agents=0, src/lib/economy/item-economy-engine.ts:367). The power curve and rarity breakdown in the same file were fixed this round to exclude unreached brackets; these two bars are the un-migrated sites of that rule. Fixed = unreached brackets render as an explicit unsampled stub, sampled zeros keep the drought look.

## Flow
- run the sim at defaults (500 players, 80 h, Lv25) - top levels unreached
- Power Curves tab -> cadence bars at those levels look like an upgrade drought
- the drought verdict calls them unmeasured, the bars call them zero

## Expected impact
Designers stop reading an unsampled endgame as an upgrade drought; nothing else reads these bars.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - unreached levels stop reading as measured zeros
Before: 2 of 2 bar charts plot unreached brackets as data (walked on the half-sampled fixture of econ-power-curve-sampled.test.tsx)
After: 0 of 2
Method: simulation - three-case walk on fixtures; a render test asserting a marker on unreached bars would decide it (not built: round budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render PowerTab on a fixture with agents=0 top brackets; assert those bars carry data-sampled=false and no '0 upgrades' title

title: Loot filter export stays Verified after the ruleset is edited
body:
## Summary
ExportPanel derives the lifecycle from persisted artifacts only, so editing rules after Generate/Wire/Verify leaves the stage pills green for a DataTable that no longer matches the ruleset.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/loot-filter/ExportPanel.tsx:51 hydrates once per ruleset.id; rule edits change ruleset.rules but not the id, and deriveLifecycle never compares the generated json against rulesetToDataTableJson(ruleset). Golden path content-drift-and-revision: an accepted artifact whose source changed is stale, not accepted. Fixed = hash the exported json into the generate artifact and show Stale when the current ruleset's hash differs.

## Flow
- Generate + Wire + Verify a ruleset
- edit any rule
- pills still read Generated/Wired/Verified; UE holds the old table

## Expected impact
Operators re-export when the rules changed instead of trusting a stale Verified. Could break: the e2e walker's expectations of the pill set.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stage pills reflect the ruleset that is actually in UE
Before: edit after verify: pills stay Verified (walked)
After: pills show Stale until re-generated
Method: simulation - walked the code path; needs a content hash on the generate artifact and a deriveLifecycle change in src/lib/loot-filter/pipeline.ts (outside this context)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: test: generate with a json hash, mutate the ruleset, rerender; assert a Stale pill. Touches src/lib/loot-filter/pipeline.ts (out-of-scope seam)

title: Economy Sourcing shows hand-typed 'actual' rarity shares as measured
body:
## Summary
RARITY_DIST carries a typed 'actual' column (Common 55%, Legendary 0%) and LUCK_SCORE 72 that RarityDistributionSection renders as observed data, while the Balance Advisor quotes only sim-measured shares.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data-economy.ts:90 types actual shares by hand; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/economy/RarityDistributionSection.tsx:21 renders them. The advisor prompt (balance-prompt.ts raritySection) was migrated to rarityEvidence() and says UNMEASURED without a run; this display is the un-migrated half. Law unmeasured-is-not-a-pass (game-economy-tuning). Fixed = read shares from the useItemEconomySessionStore result via rarityEvidence, else show UNMEASURED.

## Flow
- open Economy & Sourcing with no sim run
- rarity chart shows 'actual' 55% common, Legendary 0%
- the Mechanics advisor for the same state says rarity UNMEASURED

## Expected impact
Designers stop tuning against invented 'actual' numbers. Could break: the Economy & Sourcing layout when no run exists.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for measured rarity shares
Before: 2 readers of rarity shares: 1 derived (advisor), 1 hand-typed (sourcing)
After: 2 of 2 derived from rarityEvidence
Method: simulation - the display file is in economy/, outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render RarityDistributionSection with an empty session store; assert UNMEASURED and no 55% (owner of economy/ builds it)

title: Five set-bonus pieces name items that do not exist in the catalog
body:
## Summary
ITEM_SETS references 19 pieces; 5 (Resolve Chestplate/Helm/Greaves, Scholar Staff/Amulet) match no catalog item, yet the Balance Advisor prompt quotes those sets' bonuses as part of the item economy.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data.ts:336 onward. A probe joining ITEM_SETS piece names against DUMMY_ITEMS found 5 of 19 missing. The advisor (balance-prompt.ts Set Bonuses section) and SetsMetric count all 6 sets. Fixed = sets reference item ids and a test pins every piece resolving via resolveInventoryItem, or the two orphan sets get real items.

## Flow
- build the advisor prompt
- 'Warrior's Resolve' and 'Arcane Scholar' bonuses are judged against items the catalog never lists

## Expected impact
The advisor stops judging set power for gear that cannot drop. Could break: the Sets metric count (6 -> 4) if orphan sets are removed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every set piece resolves to a catalog item
Before: 5 of 19 pieces unresolved (probe 2026-11-08)
After: 0 of 19
Method: probe - throwaway vitest join over ITEM_SETS x DUMMY_ITEMS; the fix is a data choice (author the items vs drop the sets)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: missing = [Resolve Chestplate, Resolve Helm, Resolve Greaves, Scholar Staff, Scholar Amulet], pieces = 19
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data.ts:336
instrument: vitest: every ITEM_SETS piece name resolves in DUMMY_ITEMS (red today with 5 misses); worker decides author-items vs remove

title: Cape and Trinket items have no equipment slot
body:
## Summary
5 accessories (Travel Cloak, Echani Silk Cape, Jedi Master Mantle, Lucky Pazaak Card, Holocron Fragment) have subtypes absent from SLOT_SUBTYPES, so no slot can equip them.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data.ts:293 maps 10 slots; a probe over Weapon/Armor/Accessory subtypes found Cape and Trinket unmapped (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data-items.ts:193). These items still get accessoryStats (Evasion/Stealth, Luck/Find%) and feed the advisor as wearable gear. Fixed = add Back/Trinket slots or retype them; a test derives the subtype set from the items, not the list.

## Flow
- open the gear loadout
- no slot accepts Travel Cloak or Lucky Pazaak Card

## Expected impact
Designers see every wearable item equippable. Could break: the catalog/ loadout layout (sibling-owned) if new slots are added.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every wearable subtype has a slot
Before: 2 wearable subtypes (5 items) unmapped (probe 2026-11-08)
After: 0 unmapped
Method: probe - throwaway vitest over DUMMY_ITEMS vs SLOT_SUBTYPES; slot layout lives in catalog/ (sibling)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: subtypes of Weapon/Armor/Accessory items are all members of some SLOT_SUBTYPES list (red today: Cape, Trinket)

title: Rarity tier enumerated by hand in four places across the context
body:
## Summary
The rarity ladder is restated as RARITY_ORDER, the RM multipliers, pickAffixes' base-count map, and RARITY_LABELS; adding a tier means editing four lists that nothing cross-checks.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data-items.ts:5, src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data-items.ts:11, src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data-items.ts:29, src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/economy-simulator/constants.ts:26. Each falls back silently (?? 1, ?? 0) on an unknown tier, so a new 'Mythic' item gets Common stats and zero affixes without an error. Fixed = one RARITY_TIERS table (order, magnitude, affix count) the others derive from, and a test that every item rarity is a key.

## Flow
- add an item with rarity 'Mythic'
- weaponStats uses RM ?? 1 and pickAffixes base ?? 0 - a Common-grade item, no error

## Expected impact
Adding a tier becomes a one-line change. Could break: sibling readers of RARITY_ORDER (catalog sort).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - rarity ladder stated once
Before: 4 hand-maintained rarity enumerations, 0 cross-checks
After: 1 table, 3 derived, 1 test
Method: simulation - counted sites by grep; consolidation touches _shared (read by 2 siblings) so it needs an isolated gate run
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: an unknown rarity is reported instead of silently Common-scaled; every RARITY_ORDER key has RM and affix-count entries

title: Item Catalog and simulator tab transitions ignore reduced motion
body:
## Summary
The Item Catalog sub-tab crossfade and the simulator's skeleton/results/sub-tab transitions animate y-offsets unconditionally, while the chart stagger in the same context routes through motionSafe/useReducedMotion.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/index.tsx:114 and the TAB_TRANSITION objects at src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/economy-simulator/index.tsx:23 and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/economy-simulator/SimulationResults.tsx:22 have no reduced-motion branch; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/economy-simulator/PowerRarityTabs.tsx StaggerItem uses motionSafe(..., prefersReduced). Pair: 1 migrated pattern, 3 un-migrated sites. Fixed = wrap the three transitions with motionSafe and drop the y offset under reduced motion.

## Flow
- enable prefers-reduced-motion
- switch Item Catalog sub-tabs / run the sim
- content still slides 16px / 8px

## Expected impact
Motion-sensitive users get instant swaps. Could break: nothing functional.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - reduced motion honoured on tab swaps
Before: 3 of 4 transition sites ignore prefers-reduced-motion
After: 0 of 4
Method: simulation - read the sites; a render test mocking useReducedMotion=true and asserting the transition props would decide it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: mock framer-motion useReducedMotion -> true; assert the 3 sites pass a motionSafe-reduced transition

title: Item Catalog breadcrumb hides the active step from assistive tech
body:
## Summary
NarrativeBreadcrumb marks the active step only by colour and weight (no aria-current) and renders future steps at opacity 0.5 over text-muted.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/index.tsx:40 and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/index.tsx:43: active = accent colour + bold; future = var(--text-muted) at opacity 0.5, the alpha hack the repo's MicroLabel / --text-subtle convention replaces. Fixed = aria-current='step' on the active button and --text-subtle instead of opacity.

## Flow
- screen reader on the Item Catalog breadcrumb
- all 7 buttons announced alike, no current step

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users hear where they are; low-vision users can read future steps. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - current step announced, future steps legible
Before: 0 of 7 breadcrumb buttons expose aria-current; future steps at 0.5 opacity
After: 1 aria-current; opacity 1 with --text-subtle
Method: simulation - read the markup; the contrast figure needs theme tokens measured with lib/contrast.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: render ItemCatalog, assert exactly one breadcrumb button has aria-current; contrastRatio of text-muted at 50% vs surface from lib/contrast.ts

title: Power budget radar and affix tree are hand-typed, not derived from items
body:
## Summary
The Mechanics tab's Power Budget Radar (Iron Longsword vs Void Daggers) and Affix Probability Tree are literal constants, while the context's stated rule (balance-evidence.ts) is that evidence is derived from the items, never typed.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data-mechanics.ts:12 types radar values (Offense 0.35 / 0.92 ...) and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/_shared/data-mechanics.ts:30 types affix probabilities; neither changes when the catalog items do. Fixed = compute radar axes from item stats/affixes/rarity and the tree from the generator's actual affix distribution, or label both illustrative.

## Flow
- edit Void Daggers in the catalog
- the radar still shows Offense 92%

## Expected impact
Designers read the radar as the item's real budget only when it is. Could break: the visual layout if axes renormalise.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - mechanics visuals reflect the catalog
Before: 2 of 2 mechanics visuals hand-typed
After: 2 of 2 derived (or labelled illustrative)
Method: simulation - read the constants; what each radar axis (Economic, Utility) means is a design choice no instrument settles
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: a design decision on the meaning of each radar axis

title: Grid metric gives three of six item types the same segment colour
body:
## Summary
GridMetric's type bar colours Weapon/Armor/Consumable distinctly but Accessory, Quest and Material all fall back to ACCENT, so half the segments are indistinguishable.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/metrics/GridMetric.tsx:10 maps 3 of the 6 ALL_ITEM_TYPES. Fixed = map all six from chart-colors.

## Flow
- Features tab -> Grid metric
- Accessory/Quest/Material segments merge into one emerald block

## Expected impact
The mini bar reads as six types. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each type segment distinguishable
Before: 3 of 6 types share ACCENT
After: 6 of 6 distinct
Method: simulation - read the map; a render test counting distinct segment backgroundColors decides it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: render GridMetric over the seed catalog, assert distinct segment colours == distinct item types
